items.title: Bill Matthews Interview, 1959-03-10
items.q: That's the same old George where you're playing with me now.

ctx.x: Born and raised all of us. Born on 719 Newton Street. Every child my mother had, born and raised right there. On Newton Street. All of them born right there. None born in the Chaddawson, all of us had grannies. What you call them grannies, you know. All of them. When did you move over here? Well, my first wife and I, we separated, lived together six years. And that was after I come back from off my toe and I joined Pop. Yeah. And I come back and I settled down. And the same little, the same old drummer I got now.…

So I come up town on 4th Street, I know where George was living. I said, George, you playing Mardi Gras? He said, no, no, what happened? I said, well, you can get three pieces to go to Padre Arroyo for pop. He said, yeah, yeah, let me get three pieces. I'll get three pieces. So before I saw George, this little girl here that I got from my wife, now she was sweeping off the porch. I said, lady, can you tell me where George lives? She said, yes, right down there. I'll go get it for you. And that's where I met her,…
What was the very last job you played on drums? When the last days?

items.title: George Williams Interview, 1959-03-17
items.q: At the time, Bill Matthews and them Warren's drummer in the brass band, which is the Excelsior Band.

ctx.x: You had a brass band too, didn't you?

Well, McCullen did. But I never played in a brass band. I played with Joyce McCullen Orchestra. So, several nights, we had a rehearsal at my house on 4th Street. At the time, Bill Matthews and them Warren's drummer in the brass band, which is the Excelsior Band. You heard talk of the Excelsior Brass Band. Well, I was the youngest one in the band. I think I was 16 and a half years, 17 years old. The youngest man in the band.
Who else was in that? Who was the leader?
